source.title: Smartformer: An intelligent transformer compression framework for time-series modeling
source.authors: Xiaojian Wang; Yi-Nan Wang; Jin Yang; Ying Chen

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the article and supplemental material; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests compression on time-series Transformers and reports held-out task performance and parameter counts, a new setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study compares compression methods on EEG classification and weather forecasting. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected image models, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Accuracy and forecasting metrics are reported, but training error and train–test gaps are not.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates Transformer compression on EEG classification and weather forecasting. Its results test none of V1–V8. Changing decomposition rank is not a width sweep beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold, and improved prediction after compression does not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: among the tested methods, Smartformer improves aggregate task performance while reducing parameters across the EEG case and three Weather horizons. The authors interpret improvement after compression as mitigation of overfitting; the EEG discussion presents this tentatively. No reported train–test gaps directly establish that explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Time-series Transformer attention compression using CP-decomposition and DRL-selected ranks; evaluates forecasting and EEG classification rather than the listed natural-label generalization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The action interval changes reported performance: 50 epochs is best overall in the EEG case, while 100 epochs is consistently better across the three weather scenarios. Outcomes also differ by dataset and prediction horizon.

fits_no_version.finding: Smartformer raises mean EEG accuracy from 82.59% to 86.67% while reducing parameters from 8.69 k to 8.24 k; it improves eight subjects and ties one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive CP-decomposition can improve EEG Transformer prediction accuracy while reducing parameter count in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Smartformer lowers Weather MSE and MAE at all three horizons while reducing parameters. BTD variants attain lower errors at particular horizons but use substantially more parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The prediction-performance and parameter-count trade-off of attention compression depends on the compression method and forecasting horizon.

record.problems: The reported results do not give train error or a train–test gap, so the authors' overfitting interpretation is not directly quantified. Only two time-series model settings are studied; some backbone hyperparameters are referred to prior papers rather than restated. The supplied text reports standard deviations for EEG aggregate accuracies but no uncertainty for the weather metrics.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the 60-row cap. Table 2 contains additional subject-level and comparator accuracies; Table 3 contains additional comparator metrics; Table 4 reports parameter counts. These are not extracted individually here because they do not measure a listed version and row capacity prioritized the main outcomes and highlighted differences.

untested.parts: All: no random-label fitting or natural-versus-random-label generalization comparison.
All: no network-width sweep with an established zero-training-error threshold; decomposition-rank experiments do not establish this comparison.
All: Adam is used, but adaptive optimizers are not compared with SGD.
All: no batch-size comparison under controlled epoch budgets.
All: no dropout intervention or comparison.
All: no magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps. Gradient-based layer importance measures a different construct.
All: no memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. All 60 rows remain unlinked to V1–V8 and should be excluded from their verdict evidence. Missing train–test gaps alone would not disqualify every version; the decisive issue is the absence of their specified comparisons. The record's claim that action interval 100 is consistently best on Weather needs qualification: Table 10 reports lower horizon-192 MAE at interval 200 (0.340 versus 0.345).

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-model comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
